turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Parking was a shocker. Two laps, then some ute sitting in the disabled bay. Thanks for fitting us in, anyway.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): They're digging the front up again. Come through. Dave, and Jen, yeah?
[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm his partner. I booked it. He wasn't going to.
[SEG0004] person_3 (PATIENT): Because I'm fine. This is a waste of your arvo, seriously.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're here, so we'll use the time. Jen rang about your sleep and you being flat. Dave, your words, what's going on?
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Nothing much. Bit tired. She worries about everything.
[SEG0007] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He is not sleeping. I lie there listening to him roll around half the night, and the next day he's a write-off.
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): I sleep. Just not brilliantly. Settle down.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not brilliantly how? Getting off to sleep, waking up, or both?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): Um. Both, most nights. I lie there ages, head going. Then I'm awake again at four, sometimes half three, and that's me done.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long has it been like that?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): Couple of months. Well, actually, no. The job finished in November and it started straight after, so it's five months.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Five months. And before November you were sleeping okay?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah. Had to. Early starts at the depot. Out like a light.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): What happened with the work? Short version.
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): Council depot, forklift and the yard. Redundant. Restructure, they reckoned. Nothing going in town except night fill at the supermarket, and nah.
[SEG0017] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's put a few applications in. Then he won't look at it for a week. Just sits.
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): Eleven years I was there. Nah, twelve, I always forget, I started in the March so it's twelve. And can we not do the Centrelink thing? Those forms do my head in.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll skip Centrelink. Energy through the day, how's that?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Fine. I'm alright. Bit sluggish first thing. Everyone is.
[SEG0021] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): First thing, he says. I had Biscuit out at seven, she's the kelpie, and he hadn't even shifted. Some days it's lunch before he's really up.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Footy, the shed, your mates, walking the dog. Are you still getting any enjoyment out of that?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah, I'm fine with it. She's exaggerating. Mates are busy, that's all.
[SEG0024] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His brother offered Crows tickets and he said no. He hasn't been once. He used to live for it.
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): They've been ordinary all season. Look, I don't get the buzz. I put the telly on and I can't be bothered. The thing in the shed's just sitting there half finished.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): So the interest has dropped off. Not only the energy.
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): If you're writing it down, yeah. Don't make it a huge thing.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Under that, the mood. Sad, flat, teary, short with people?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Not sad. I'm not sitting there crying. Flat, if you need a word. I get snappy with her sometimes. Not proud of it.
[SEG0030] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The quiet worries me more than the snappy. He'll just go still.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Appetite? Weight? Any change you've noticed?
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Appetite's fine. I eat.
[SEG0033] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He pushes it round the plate. Last night half the snags were left. It's been like that for weeks, don't let him tell you otherwise.
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): I wasn't hungry last night. One night. I eat enough. I'm not wasting away.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not writing wasting away. I am noting the two of you don't agree, and I'll park it. Any neck pain, headaches, dizzy spells?
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): Neck's a bit sore off the couch. No dizzy spells. I chuck a couple of Panadol and the neck comes good.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ordinary Panadol, paracetamol? How often?
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah, not the strong ones. Couple of times a week if it's nagging. Not daily.
[SEG0039] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the water tablet. He still takes that every morning, tell the doctor.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you know the name and the dose?
[SEG0041] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's indapamide. His water tablet. Two and a half milligrams. Chemist wrote it on the repeat.
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): No, it's five. Five milligrams. Little white tablets, I read the box last week. She's got it wrong.
[SEG0043] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Cupboard box says two point five. You were half asleep.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm not picking a winner between two point five and five while you argue. Bring the actual box next time, or a photo of the label. Anything else you take regularly?
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah, I'll bring the box. That's it otherwise, the water tablet and the odd Panadol. I don't like pills.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Other history. Blood pressure, diabetes, asthma, any operations?
[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): Blood pressure, yep, that's the point of the water tablet. Been years. No diabetes, no asthma, and I've never had an operation.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Last you heard, was the pressure behaving?
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): Chemist reckoned it was good. Don't ask me the number, it's gone. Ages back.
[SEG0050] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You should know about his mum. She was treated for depression for years.
[SEG0051] person_3 (PATIENT): That was after my brother. Long time ago. Mum's fine now. We don't have to unpack it.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): We won't unpack it. Helps to know it's been in the family. Do you smoke, Dave?
[SEG0053] person_3 (PATIENT): Never. Can't stand the smell.
[SEG0054] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He has a beer with tea, though. Say that bit.
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): How many on a normal night?
[SEG0056] person_3 (PATIENT): Two. Light beers. Same as when I was working. I'm not drinking to get to sleep.
[SEG0057] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two's about right. I'll agree with him there.
[SEG0058] person_2 (DOCTOR): Who's at home?
[SEG0059] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Just us and the dog. She sticks to him, which he pretends means nothing.
[SEG0060] person_3 (PATIENT): Dogs do that. Can we get on with it.
[SEG0061] person_2 (DOCTOR): One straight question, and it's routine, not me deciding you're unsafe. Any thoughts about hurting yourself, or hoping you don't wake up?
[SEG0062] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Definitely not. I'm not that bloke, I'd never do that to her. I just can't be stuffed, that's different.
[SEG0063] person_2 (DOCTOR): Clear, thank you. If that ever changes, you don't sit on it. You tell Jen, and you come here or you go to emergency the same day.
[SEG0064] person_3 (PATIENT): Yep. Won't happen. Heard you.
[SEG0065] person_2 (DOCTOR): Arm out, I'll check the pressure. One thirty-eight over eighty-six. Pulse is seventy-eight... no, ignore that, last patient's still on the screen. Yours is sixty-eight.
[SEG0066] person_3 (PATIENT): See? Normal. Told you both.

[SEG0067] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pressure and pulse are normal, yes. On looking at you, you're kempt, speech is ordinary, no restlessness. Affect's a bit flat. Nothing acute, and I won't put you through a full examination.
[SEG0068] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is it depression, then? Just tell us.

[SEG0069] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll think out loud, and I don't want you grabbing one word. Losing a job after twelve years can knock sleep, get-up-and-go and interest, and sometimes that is a drawn-out adjustment, sometimes a depressive episode. I cannot split those two today. I am not stamping a diagnosis on you.
[SEG0070] person_3 (PATIENT): Right. So I'm fine.
[SEG0071] person_2 (DOCTOR): I didn't say fine. No label yet is not the same as fine. Things that mimic this, a low thyroid, anaemia, sleep apnoea if the snoring had suddenly got wild. Has it?
[SEG0072] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He snores a bit. He always has. Not worse. I moved rooms because of the tossing, not the noise.
[SEG0073] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then no bloods today, and no sleep study. I am not concluding any of that. We'll see how a few weeks go before I order anything.
[SEG0074] person_3 (PATIENT): And no tablets. I don't want to start something.

[SEG0075] person_2 (DOCTOR): If we start one later, it'd be sertraline. A lot of GPs go straight to fifty milligrams. Actually I'd start you at twenty-five if we ever do it, not this afternoon. I want to see you again first.
[SEG0076] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So what is he meant to do? Don't say warm milk.

[SEG0077] person_2 (DOCTOR): No milk. Out of bed the same time every day, curtains open, phone not in the bed, and the couch is not for sleeping. If you're still awake after about twenty minutes, get up, do something dull, go back when you're sleepy. That's on you, Dave, not on Jen to police it.
[SEG0078] person_3 (PATIENT): Bit of homework. I'll have a crack. Phone thing, we'll see.
[SEG0079] person_2 (DOCTOR): A crack is enough. Book at reception for three weeks, back here with me. Bring that indapamide box.
[SEG0080] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): If he slides before then he will not ring you. What do I do?

[SEG0081] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the mood drops sharply, or either of you is worried, don't wait out the three weeks. Ring us and we'll fit him in. And the harm thoughts, that's same day, no debate. Go on, get the dog out of the ute.

spec.situation: Adult with poor sleep, low energy and loss of interest for months after a job loss or bereavement; partner or parent speaks for them; patient says 'I'm fine' then partly opens up; denies thoughts of self-harm clearly (doctor asks gently); medication discussed but not started today.
features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

bad.reason: Patient says energy is fine; low energy was not reported by patient.
bad.text: low energy (category=constitutional, status=present, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Neck soreness and Panadol supported; frequency applies to Panadol use, not clearly soreness frequency.
bad.text: neck soreness (category=musculoskeletal, status=present, severity=mild, frequency=a couple of times a week, temporality=current, body_site=neck, relieving_factors=Panadol, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Low energy is recorded wrongly: the patient denied low energy ('Fine... Bit sluggish first thing'), while the partner reported he often stays in bed until lunch before really being up.
The patient described his insomnia in more detail: takes a long time to get to sleep because his 'head [is] going', then wakes again at 3:30-4:00 am and is done for the night.
Before November he was sleeping okay, with early starts at the depot and being 'out like a light'.
Asked-and-answered negative finding missing: before job loss he had no sleep problem; sleep was okay prior to November.
Asked-and-answered negative finding missing: no headaches.

Medication discrepancy detail missing: indapamide is taken every morning for blood pressure, but the dose is disputed between 2.5 mg (partner) and 5 mg (patient); the doctor deferred deciding until the box/photo is brought.
Past history detail missing: no known operations ever.
History detail missing: last blood pressure check was at the chemist, reportedly 'good', but the patient does not know the number and it was a while ago.
Denied finding missing: the patient denied ever smoking because he cannot stand the smell.
Self-harm denial detail missing: he also denied passive death wish/hoping he would not wake up ('No. Definitely not.').
Examination detail missing: the doctor stated there was 'nothing acute' and did not perform a full examination.
Assessment detail missing: possible mimics discussed were low thyroid, anaemia, and sleep apnoea if snoring had suddenly worsened.
Asked-and-answered negative finding missing: snoring has not suddenly worsened; he snores a bit and always has, and partner changed rooms because of tossing, not noise.
Plan detail missing: no blood tests today and no sleep study; the doctor is not concluding thyroid/anaemia/sleep apnoea and will wait a few weeks before ordering anything.

Patient denied being sad, stating he was 'not sad' and not just 'not crying'.
Patient denied low energy, saying energy through the day was 'fine' apart from being 'a bit sluggish first thing.'
Doctor specifically advised to ring the clinic and they would fit him in if things worsened before the 3-week review; this escalation advice to call the clinic is not fully captured.
